change: Cache npm dependencies keyed on package-lock.json with an `npm-default` fallback key; `lint` pushes the cache, other jobs pull it.
expected_effect: Fewer repeated package downloads per job; shorter `npm ci` phase. Effect is measured as runner-minutes (proxy) and pipeline duration (measured).
risk: Low. A stale cache cannot change what is installed because npm ci still verifies against the lockfile; a cache miss only falls back to a full download.

change: Documentation-only changes skip lint/test/build. An explicit `classify` job diffs the whole pushed range with git, fails safe to "code", and triggers the matching child pipeline (ci/child-*.gitlab-ci.yml). secret_detection always runs in the parent.
expected_effect: Three jobs avoided per docs-only pipeline at the cost of one short classify job. Effect is counted (jobs executed) and measured (duration).
risk: Low. Misclassification fails toward running everything; the changed-path list is printed in the classify job log; the docs allow-list is unit-tested (src/classify.js). Replaced GitLab `rules:changes`, which judged a merge commit by its first parent and skipped tests on a code change (showcase pipeline 2994150067).

change: workflow:rules so a commit on a branch with an open MR runs one pipeline instead of two.
expected_effect: Halves pipelines for MR commits. Counted at the project pipeline list; not part of the per-run comparison.

change: Measure energy per run and calculate SCI.
expected_effect: UNKNOWN until runner energy telemetry or a validated model with a documented boundary is available.
risk: Risk of overclaiming. Not applied: no defensible energy input exists for GitLab shared runners.

change: Run lint, test and build in ONE job (ci/consolidated.gitlab-ci.yml) instead of three. Nothing is skipped; no cache; no classify job. One change, isolated.
expected_effect: Derived from the measured arms: each job here spends ~12-15 s on provisioning, image pull and checkout against ~2 s of real work, so removing two jobs should cut runner-minutes by roughly a third for every change class.
risk: Low. Same commands, same gates, same order. Loses per-job parallelism, which this project does not use, and per-job failure granularity (a failing lint stops the job before tests; the log still shows which step failed).
